bib.title: DistilBERT, a distilled version of BERT: smaller, faster, cheaper and lighter
bib.venue: preprint (EMC^2: 5th Edition Co-located with NeurIPS'19 per footer; arXiv v4, 1 Mar 2020)

question: Can a smaller general-purpose BERT-like model be pre-trained with knowledge distillation so that it keeps most of BERT's language understanding while being smaller and faster?
hypothesis: Distillation during pre-training, with a triple loss and teacher-based initialisation, yields a student that fine-tunes well on many tasks at lower size and latency.
contributions: Pre-training-phase knowledge distillation for a general-purpose student (40% smaller, 60% faster, 97% of GLUE performance)
Triple loss combining masked LM, distillation and cosine-distance losses
Proof-of-concept on-device question answering app and comparative on-device study

method.summary: A 6-layer student with BERT's architecture (token-type embeddings and pooler removed) is initialised from every second teacher layer and pre-trained on the BERT corpus with a linear combination of soft-target distillation, masked LM and cosine embedding losses. It is then fine-tuned on GLUE, IMDb and SQuAD v1.1.
method.task: pre-training distillation of a masked language model, then fine-tuning for GLUE, IMDb, SQuAD

datasets.name: English Wikipedia + Toronto Book Corpus
datasets.source: same corpus as original BERT (Zhu et al. 2015)
datasets.preprocessing: dynamic masking, no next sentence prediction

models.name: DistilBERT
models.architecture: BERT architecture, token-type embeddings and pooler removed, layers reduced by a factor of 2
models.init_from: teacher, taking one layer out of two
models.layers: inferred: half of BERT-base's layers (the paper says 'reduced by a factor of 2'; no number printed)

other.note: GLUE results as reported by the authors; baseline computed with jiant

training.objective: linear combination of Lce (soft-target distillation, sum_i t_i*log(s_i), softmax temperature T on teacher and student, T=1 at inference), Lmlm (masked LM) and Lcos (cosine embedding loss aligning student and teacher hidden states)
training.batch_size: up to 4K examples per batch via gradient accumulation

other.recipe: best practices from Liu et al. 2019 (RoBERTa): large batches, dynamic masking, no NSP
other.second_distillation_step: DistilBERT (D): fine-tuned on SQuAD with an extra distillation term from a BERT fine-tuned on SQuAD

other.cpu: Intel Xeon E5-2690 v3 Haswell @2.9GHz, batch size 1, full pass over STS-B dev set
other.phone: iPhone 7 Plus, QA app, excluding tokenization

metrics.name: GLUE macro-score
metrics.definition: average of individual task scores on dev sets

metrics.name: Inference time
metrics.definition: seconds for a full pass of STS-B dev on CPU, batch size 1

eval.protocol: GLUE: medians of 5 runs with different seeds; no ensembling or multi-task. Other tables do not state runs.

availability.code: Transformers library (github.com/huggingface/transformers); swift-coreml-transformers for the app

evidence.quote: DistilBERT was trained on 8 16GB V100 GPUs for approximately 90 hours.

limits: Pre-training hyperparameters (optimizer, learning rate, steps, temperature T, loss weights, sequence length) and fine-tuning settings are not given.
Speed measured on one CPU at batch size 1 and one phone; seeds reported only for GLUE.
Per-task drops are uneven (RTE -9.4, CoLA -5.0) but the headline is the average.
Ablation reports GLUE macro-score only, one configuration each, no seed spread.
Text and Table 2 disagree on the SQuAD figure for the second-distillation variant (79.8/70.4 vs 79.1/86.9).
Pruning and quantization are not combined; stated as orthogonal.

terms.definition: a compression technique in which a compact model - the student - is trained to reproduce the behaviour of a larger model - the teacher - or an ensemble of models

lineage.work: Distilling the knowledge in a neural network
lineage.quote: Following Hinton et al. [2015] we used a softmax-temperature

lineage.note: large batches, dynamic masking, no NSP
lineage.quote: We applied best practices for training BERT model recently proposed in Liu et al. [2019].

lineage.work: Well-read students learn better (Turc et al.)
lineage.note: pretrains small students with the original objective then distils at fine-tuning; paper claims added distillation signal helps

lineage.work: Michel et al. 2019 (Are sixteen heads really better than one?)

figures.caption: Ablation study. Variations are relative to the model trained with triple loss and teacher weights initialization.
figures.why: Shows teacher init and distillation losses account for most of the quality
